# 🎵🎨🧠 Gold Coast Events Digest: 11–17 May 2026

## ⭐ HEADLINE EVENT OF THE WEEK

### 1. Blues on Broadbeach 2026 — 25th Anniversary Festival
**📅 Thu 14 – Sun 17 May 2026**
**📍 Broadbeach City Centre (multiple stages, streets, parks & venues)**
**🎟️ Mostly FREE (Sunday Ticket ticketed) | [bluesonbroadbeach.com](https://bluesonbroadbeach.com)**
**Category: Concert / Music**

Blues on Broadbeach returns for its 25th annual celebration from 14–17 May 2026, bringing together an incredible mix of international icons and homegrown talent across multiple indoor and outdoor stages — one of Australia's largest music festivals, set in the vibrant heart of Broadbeach.

The 2026 lineup includes Ian Moss, Ruthie Foster, The Bamboos, MonoNeon, Robert Finley, The Lachy Doley Trio, Kevin Borich Express, Grace Cummings, Daddy Long Legs, WILSN, Hussy Hicks, and many more.

A massive 19 stages pop up around the precinct, with the biggest spread across Kurrawa and Victoria Park. Expect restaurant and bar takeovers with live soundtracks, plus ticketed events featuring artists like Frank Sultana and Scottie Miller at venues like Roosevelt Lounge.

On Sunday 17 May, the Kurrawa Park precinct comes alive with The Teskey Brothers making their Blues on Broadbeach debut as part of the ticketed Sunday Ticket event, joined by Grammy-winning artist Judith Hill and Ash Grunwald.

Blues on Broadbeach is predominantly a non-ticketed event, with multiple indoor and outdoor stages for everyone to enjoy. The Sunday Ticket (for Kurrawa Park on Sunday) is the main paid element. A perfect event for music lovers who like wandering between stages and discovering new artists.

Multiple free exhibitions are currently running at HOTA Gallery, including shows running through to 31 May 2026, and others through to July and August 2026.

In April 2026, HOTA Gallery presented a major exhibition drawn from the White Rabbit Collection in Sydney — one of the world's most significant and influential holdings of contemporary Chinese art. This is still showing during our week. The HOTA Gallery is free-entry and attracts a thoughtful, creative crowd. Well worth a visit before or after one of the live events.

## 🧠 PUBLIC LECTURES & INTELLECTUAL TALKS

### 6. Bond University Faculty of Law Twilight Seminar: "The Anti-System Trump — And What Do We Do About It?"
**📅 Mon 11 May 2026, 5:00pm–6:30pm (seminar starts 5:30pm, refreshments from 5pm)**
**📍 Bond University, Faculty of Law (Building 4), Level 3, Room 3_41, Robina**
**🎟️ Free (vegan, GF & dairy-free refreshments provided) | [bond.edu.au/event/10657](https://bond.edu.au/event/10657/twilight-seminar-anti-system-trump-and-what-do-we-do-about-it)**
**Category: Public Lecture**

The abstract: Trump has done it again — not merely by shifting policy, but by signalling that the United States is willing to act against the very system it once built. Trade rules are no longer treated as constraints; they are invoked selectively, reshaped opportunistically, and discarded when inconvenient. This seminar argues that US trade policy under Donald Trump is now openly anti-systemic.

A free, accessible Faculty of Law public seminar — open to the community. An excellent night for anyone interested in geopolitics, international law, systems thinking, or the Trump era's global impact. Light refreshments included.

### 7. Bond University High School Model United Nations (BUHMUN) 2026
**📅 Tue 12 – Wed 13 May 2026**
**📍 Bond University Gold Coast Campus, Robina**
**🎟️ Registration required (waitlist) | [bond.edu.au](https://bond.edu.au/study/experience-bond-for-yourself/high-school-student-experiences/experience-a-study-area/bond-0)**
**Category: Public Lecture / Community**

BUHMUN 2026 takes place on Tuesday 12 and Wednesday 13 May at Bond University's Gold Coast Campus. The conference is an incredible opportunity for future world leaders to develop their skills alongside students from all over. It allows students to extend what they learn at school about Sustainable Development Goals and interact with students who share the same interests and passions. Primarily targeted at high school students, but great for educators, community members or curious onlookers interested in debate, diplomacy, and global issues.
